title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is manuscript page 696 (archive page 75), in the part of the 'suite à la Longue Marche' where Grothendieck builds explicit group schemes over a base S (2 invertible on the previous page). These group schemes model automorphisms of a pair of generators ρ, σ. Here σ is clearly involutive-type, ε2 and ε3 are sign characters, and M is an abelian lattice-type group scheme. The setting looks like a genus-1, modular-group (SL2-type) situation.

The previous page shows three things:
- Z_{ρ,σ} is smooth of relative dimension 2.
- Z_{ρ,σ} sits in an extension 1 → Z^{+0}_{ρ,σ} (≅ G_a) → Z_{ρ,σ} → O_12^* → 1, where O_12^* is a group scheme of 'units' parametrised by (ν2, ν3, ν'', …).
- A line L_0^♮ = {λ·λ_0} ⊂ M maps into Z_{ρ,σ} by ℓ ↦ (int(ℓ), 1), which corresponds to ((1−ρ_M)ℓ, (1−σ_M)ℓ).

This page proceeds as follows.
- (145) That map identifies L_0^♮ with Z^{+0}_{ρ,σ}, the G_a kernel.
- (146) The quotient V_{ρ,σ} := Z_{ρ,σ}/L_0^♮ is therefore isomorphic to O_12^*.
- (147) Define G_{ρ,σ} := (Z_{ρ,σ}·S^+)/L_0^♮. This is the amalgamated product (pushout of group extensions) of Z_{ρ,σ} and S^+ along the common normal subgroup L_0^♮. Here S^+ is the ambient group containing ρ, σ and M, presumably a semidirect product of M with a discrete or finite part.
- (148) This gives a morphism of extensions: 1→L_0^♮→Z→V→1 maps into 1→S^+→G→V→1, with the identity on V.
- (149) There is a canonical section O_12^* → Z_{ρ,σ} ≅ Σ_{ρ,σ}, sending μ to (μ, ξ_0 = ν''(3λ_1), η_0 = 0).
- (150) Hence both groups are semidirect products: Z ≅ O_12^* ⋉ L_0^♮ and G ≅ O_12^* ⋉ S^+.
- The action on L_0^♮ goes through a character O_12^* → G_m acting by homotheties.
- (151) The action on S^+ is u_μ(ρ) = λ_1^ν ρ, u_μ(σ) = (μ^{1/2}?) σ, and u_μ(x) = μx for x ∈ M. Here ν = 3ν'' − ν_3, consistent with the next page.
- Margin: a subgroup G^♮_{ρ,σ} = O_12^*·S^♮ ⊂ G_{ρ,σ} is introduced.

The purpose is to get an explicit presentation of the group G_{ρ,σ}, of its character χ: G → O_12^*, and of its subgroups. The next page treats N_ρ, the stabiliser of ρ up to the sign ε3, and checks that χ restricted to N_ρ is onto.
errors: The pushout in (147) needs L_0^♮ to be normal in both Z and S^+, with compatible conjugation actions. This is implicit, given (144) where L_0^♮ → Z is ℓ ↦ int(ℓ).
The formula for u_μ(σ) is partly struck out or ambiguous in the manuscript (a μ^{1/2} factor appears). Whether it is exactly μ^{1/2}σ cannot be confirmed from the image.

ideas.what: Amalgamating two group extensions along a common normal subgroup L_0 (pushout G = (Z·S^+)/L_0), giving a morphism of extensions over the same quotient V
ideas.modern_name: pushout of group extensions / amalgamated (central-type) product
ideas.where_published: general extension formalism appears in SGA 7 / Giraud-style contexts; this specific construction is not known to be published

ideas.what: Canonical section of Z → O_12^*, giving semidirect product decompositions of Z and G and an explicit action of O_12^* on ρ, σ and M
ideas.modern_name: split extension / semidirect product presentation of an automorphism group scheme

ideas.what: Overall programme: group-scheme (over S with 2 invertible) models of automorphisms of the generator pair (ρ, σ) in a genus-1/modular setting, with a 'units' group O_12^* acting as a cyclotomic-type character
ideas.modern_name: algebraic models of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type actions in genus 1 (cf. relative completion of SL2(Z), GT in genus 1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto, Enriquez (elliptic GT) — loose analogy only
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses Galois/Teichmüller themes; these explicit computations appear unpublished

missed.claim: This page is one step in an explicit, unpublished construction of group schemes G_{ρ,σ} and G^♮_{ρ,σ}, defined over bases where 2 is invertible. They carry a character to a group scheme O_12^* and act on generators ρ, σ and a lattice M. The construction does not seem to have been written up or compared with later algebraic treatments of genus-1 Teichmüller/Galois actions.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may give a concrete scheme-theoretic model, with 2 and 3 entering via O_12^*, for the 'arithmetic' symmetries of the modular group. A specialist could compare it with relative completions of SL2(Z) or with elliptic GT. However, the page itself is only routine extension bookkeeping.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine manipulations: a pushout of extensions, a splitting, and a semidirect product description. Its interest lies only in being part of a larger unpublished explicit construction whose exact meaning cannot be fully pinned down from this page alone.
transcription_corrections: In (151), the coefficient 'λ_1^{6ν^4}' should most likely read 'λ_1^{ν}ρ (en dernière expl.)'. The next page has u_μ(ρ) = λ_1^ν ρ with ν = 3ν'' − ν_3.
In (148), the vertical arrows are inclusions (∩) and the right vertical arrow is an identity (∥), as transcribed.
In the margin, read 'G^♮_{ρ,σ} = O_12^*·S^♮|M ⊂ G_{ρ,σ}'. The subscript under O_12^* seems to be ρ,σ-related and is uncertain.
